data.title: Page Metadata
data.tagline: Information about a page that is read outside its visible body
data.learningOutcome: You can split page metadata checks by browser, search, sharing, and installation instead of treating one successful field as proof that everything is complete.
data.description: Page metadata lives in the document head and is read separately by browsers, search systems, sharing platforms, or install surfaces. It is not one completion switch; inspect the relevant field and rendered result for each consumer.

learning.assumes: You have seen a browser tab, a search result, or a link preview in a chat.
learning.outcome: You can split page metadata checks by browser, search, sharing, and installation instead of treating one successful field as proof that everything is complete.

distinctions.label: Open Graph
distinctions.explanation: Page Metadata is the broad group of head information; Open Graph specifically describes a shared-link card's title, description, image, and URL.

distinctions.label: Title Tag
distinctions.explanation: Title Tag is one concrete title field in page metadata; Page Metadata also covers information for search, sharing, and installation.

explanation.title: Head fields produce different results
explanation.text: The title affects the browser tab, a description may help form a search snippet, Open Graph fields feed a link preview, and a Manifest describes an install entry. They relate to the body but are not body content.

explanation.title: Verify each consumer's actual result
explanation.text: Ask who reads a field, then check the field, resource URL, and final presentation. A correct one only proves that its corresponding consumer received usable information.

data.boundary: Page Metadata is the broad category; it does not replace Title Tag, Open Graph, or Web App Manifest. A missing share image needs share fields, while a wrong installed launch path needs the Manifest.

lessonPractice.title: The browser tab title is correct, but a shared link has no image. Where should you look first?

options.label: Inspect metadata read by sharing platforms, add the matching image, and retest with a real preview
options.feedback: Correct. Consumers read different fields, so a correct tab title does not prove that the share image exists or is reachable.

options.label: Rewrite the first paragraph so the platform can automatically find an image in the body
options.feedback: Page content is not the same as sharing metadata and cannot replace checking the fields that feed the preview card.

options.label: Change the Favicon because every page image comes from it
options.feedback: A Favicon mainly identifies the site in browser surfaces; it is not the main image field for a share card.

data.agentPrompt: List this page's metadata separately for the browser tab, search snippet, shared link, and install entry, and add only the missing field for each consumer. Verify with page source, search output, and a real share preview; do not treat metadata as one indivisible completion flag.

references.title: Control your snippets in search results
